samples.summary: The dry-run URL fidelity claim is never checked against the real HttpClient — the client is fully mocked and the expected URLs are hand-written duplicates
samples.evidence: read-dry-run.test.ts:26 replaces the whole `HttpClient` module with a stub class, so no test in the suite ever observes the URL the real client builds. cells.ts:20-32 hand-builds `/documents/{doc}/tabs/{tab}/cells[?range=...|/{ref}]` and its comment claims it "encodes the range exactly as `HttpClient.getCells` does, so the printed URL is the URL that would have been fetched" — but the test asserts only against literal strings (`${BASE}/documents/doc-1/tabs/tab-1/cells?range=A1%3AC10`), which are a second hand-written copy of the same path. If `HttpClient.getCells` (http-client.ts:340-346) later changes its query name, encoding, or path shape, every assertion here still passes while the preview lies about what would be fetched — exactly the drift the duplication creates. A test that spies on `globalThis.fetch` and runs the same command WITHOUT `--dry-run`, then compares the two URLs, would pin the property the comments assert; I grepped packages/cli/test for `getCells` and `api/v1/workspaces` and found only tabs.test.ts, config.test.ts and this new file, none of which exercise the real client's URL construction.

samples.summary: No test covers --dry-run when config resolution fails: `docs get` and `tabs list` call getConfig/printDryRun outside the try/catch
samples.evidence: docs.ts:125-128 and tabs.ts:14-17 evaluate `getConfig(opts)` before the `try`, unlike `docs list` (docs.ts:73-83) which is inside it. The new tests always pass `--server/--workspace/--api-key`, so the path where `resolveConfig` throws (missing workspace/profile) is never exercised for these two commands — a throw there escapes the action handler instead of producing the `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope the other commands emit. No test in packages/cli/test drives a dry-run without a resolvable config.

samples.summary: Test file is framed as "--dry-run on read commands" but several read commands still fetch under --dry-run and none of them is covered
samples.evidence: grep for `opts.dryRun` across packages/cli/src/commands shows no dry-run branch in `notes list` (notes.ts:32), `notes get` (notes.ts:73), `slides list` (slides.ts:37), `slides get` (slides.ts:78), `files list` (files.ts:76), `files get` (files.ts:102) or the `api-keys` read commands (api-keys.ts:26). The new suite's own premise — "a preview that reaches the network burns rate limit and emits an access log the caller was told would not happen" — applies identically to those, yet no test asserts it for them, so the regression the file guards against is only pinned for docs/cells/tabs. (Whether those commands should also gain the branch is the correctness lens; the test-side point is that the suite's title over-promises its coverage.)
searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts / slides.ts / files.ts headers via grep output

samples.summary: The reworked empty-string fail-safe test now largely duplicates the existing "push to main is never filtered" case and no longer exercises the fall-through it documents
samples.evidence: After the change the env is `{ WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS: "", GITHUB_EVENT_NAME: "push", GITHUB_REF_NAME: "main" }`, which hits the deploy-gate short-circuit at changed-areas.mjs:530 — the same branch already asserted at changed-areas.test.mjs:223-230. It still distinguishes the bug (if `""` were consumed, the reason would be "not valid JSON", failing the new /push to main/ match), so it is not vacuous, but the comment's claim that the empty string "is ignored so resolution continues and fails safe" is now only proven as far as the very next branch: nothing asserts that on a NON-main event an empty `WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS` falls through to git-based classification rather than to a bogus `{full: undefined}`. A hermetic fixture repo (the file already builds them, e.g. twoCommitRepo at line 661) plus a non-main event would restore that without depending on the working tree.

verdict.reason: The factual part of the finding checks out: read-dry-run.test.ts:20-27 mocks the whole HttpClient module, and I found no test anywhere in the repo that pins the real client's cells URL (searched `cells\?range`, `tabs/.../cells`, `api/v1/workspaces`, `globalThis.fetch|stubGlobal('fetch')|new HttpClient`, and every `dry-run` test under packages/cli/test; the only real-fetch tests are docs-content.test.ts:306-336, which asserts an error body, and output.test.ts:283-290, which runs `sheets cells get` through the real client but never inspects the URL). However, this is not a blocking test-adequacy defect. The code under test — the dry-run branch in cells.ts:20-32 and printDryRun in dry-run.ts:12-24 — is real and unmocked in this suite: a wrong query name, wrong encoding or wrong path shape breaks read-dry-run.test.ts:126/137/148, and removing the dry-run guard makes the getCells/getCell counters fire at :122/:133/:144. So the assertions are failable, not vacuous, and the mocked collaborator is exactly the one that must not run during a preview. The preview and the client also agree today (dry-run.ts:13 vs http-client.ts:82-85; cells.ts:25-29 vs http-client.ts:340-346), so no live mismatch is being hidden. What is genuinely missing is a cross-check guarding against future drift between two duplicated URL builders — "coverage could be broader" (minor), which the rubric explicitly says not to raise as a blocker when the changed behavior already has meaningful coverage.
